objective: Minimise pooling detour cost per additional rider by only accepting a new order when the driver's route already passes very close to BOTH its pickup and its drop-off, so the extra rider is essentially free to serve.
description: For a loaded car the skill computes the minimum true insertion detour across all consecutive anchor pairs, hard-rejects any order where either endpoint is far from the route or the combined detour exceeds a pressure-scaled fraction of one solo trip, then ranks survivors by the ratio party / (epsilon + best_detour) — a pure efficiency ratio that gives near-infinite value to genuinely free inserts and collapses quickly as detour grows. The noop floor is set high enough that a loaded car will not accept an order whose detour ratio merely beats zero; it must beat a floor that rises with fill and falls with demand pressure, so thin-fleet high-pressure scenes still serve riders while well-supplied scenes hold out for free pools. An empty car always accepts, ranked by inverse fetch distance, since there is no pooling detour to protect.
fitness_rationale: The ratio directly measures the skill's core trade-off: completed riders in the numerator rewards throughput while the detour penalty in the denominator suppresses pooling cost, so variants that serve more riders with less added route length score higher.
mechanism: patience / option value: a high noop floor that makes waiting a real choice, so the driver holds out for a genuinely dual-free insert rather than accepting any feasible order; the score is the ratio of party size to marginal detour cost, gated by a strict dual-proximity hard reject
differs_from: closest to backhaul_adaptive_gate_dualfree, which gates on the tail-fetch from the last drop-off only; this skill instead measures the true insertion detour at every anchor position and sets the noop floor as a function of current fill AND demand pressure, so a lightly-loaded car in a low-pressure scene waits harder (higher floor) while a full car in a high-pressure scene lowers its patience threshold to protect throughput — the gate tightness and the noop floor both move together with pressure rather than being fixed

audit.reason: The table shows the skill doing exactly what was promised: detour/order is near-zero across all scenarios (0.01–0.26), confirming the dual-proximity gate is rejecting high-detour orders. Completed riders are high (2363–7727) and fitness values are strongly positive (+1687 to +4798), consistent with the efficiency-ratio objective rewarding throughput at minimal detour cost. The pressure-adaptive noop floor and gate_frac mechanism are consistent with the observed variation in service rate (0.332–0.885) across different fleet/demand conditions.
audit.evidence: The detour/order column (0.01–0.26 across all six scenarios) is the decisive column: it confirms the hard-reject gate is suppressing pooling detour as designed, while completed (2363–7727) confirms throughput is preserved.
